(a) Buildings of any type construction or occupancy of 5,000 square feet or more per floor, or buildings of two or more stories in height shall be protected throughout by an approved supervised automatic sprinkler system installed in accordance with the current State of Georgia adopted edition of the NFPA 13, as modified, Standards for the Installation of Sprinkler Systems. A sprinkler control valve and water flow device shall be provided for each floor. The building official or the Douglas County Fire Department may additionally require the installation of a water-based fire protection system and/or smoke detection system, where the public interest, the health and welfare of the fire fighters, or the protection of human life, would be protected by the same, due to the type of construction, hazard of content, limited access to the structure, or other safety factors.
(b) All hotels, motels, dormitories, apartments, lodging facilities, townhouses, rooming houses, all residential board and care facilities, and all day care facilities, and all personal care facilities with more than seven clients as defined by NFPA 101, Life Safety Code shall be protected by an approved supervised automatic sprinkler system installed in accordance with the current State of Georgia adopted edition with amendments for NFPA 13 or 13R, as modified or amended, Standards for the Installation of Sprinkler Systems in Residential Occupancies up to and including three stories in height. Based on the type of construction and the tenants' ability to evacuate, the building official or his designee shall designate which system is best suited in each situation. Residential occupancies exceeding three stories in height shall be protected by an approved automatic sprinkler system installed in accordance with NFPA 13.
(c) Existing buildings, when required to have automatic sprinkler protection by subsections (a) or (b) above, shall be retrofitted for automatic sprinklers as required by the building official or his designee in accordance with NFPA 13 or 13R, when:
(1) A building is renovated, and the cost of renovation exceeds 50 percent of the latest approved tax assessed value of the building; or
(2) There is a change in occupancy classification.
Whenever such retrofitting is required by this section, the buildings shall be required to upgrade to meet all current codes, standards, and ordinances for fire protection and life safety systems, and the owner shall have the system inspected and tested in accordance with NFPA 25, as modified, Standards for the Inspection, Testing and Maintenance of Water-based Fire Protection Systems.
Exceptionally, existing buildings located in the historic district or on any historic site may use standards set forth by chapter 48 of the City Code, as the city may amend from time to time. As a further exception, for existing buildings located within the historic district and lying south of Broad Street, north of Spring Street, east of Club Drive, and west of Duncan Street, installation of sprinklers shall not be required.
(d) Automatic fire sprinkler systems shall be installed in all newly constructed multifamily dwellings, regardless of the type of construction or square feet. In addition, automatic fire sprinkler systems shall be installed in all new single-family and duplex dwellings, regardless of the type of construction, whenever side yard setbacks are to be 7.5 linear feet or less; said systems shall conform to the NFPA standard 13R, current edition, Standard for the Installation of Sprinkler Systems in One- and Two-Family Dwellings and Manufactured Homes. "New", for the purpose of this section, includes any addition to existing buildings, whether vertical or horizontal; any existing building or structure shall be subject to this requirement where there is substantial renovation due to fire or other hazard of serious consequence. For purposes of this paragraph, "substantial" means any construction project involving exits or internal/external features of such buildings or structure costing more than or equal to 50 percent of the building's or structure's gross tax assessed value at the time of such renovation, repair, remodeling, or replacement.
(e) Where required, post indicator valves (PIV) and fire department connections (FDC) shall be located at or near the main entry to the site but no closer than one and one-half times the height of the building. Appropriate signage shall be provided to designate PIV and FDC connections. Minimum diameter of FDC coupling shall be two and one-half-inch.
(f) All water-based fire protection systems shall have electronically supervised monitoring; all fire alarm systems installed in commercial buildings shall be supervised at all times, and shall include installation of horns and strobes; and pull stations shall be provided at all required exits as designated by the Douglas County Fire Department.
(g) No person shall shut off or disable any automatic fire sprinkler system or fire alarm system, and no owner, occupant, or resident of any building shall disarm or allow disarming of such systems. Exceptionally, such systems may be shut off in order to perform maintenance work on the systems during the time that qualified maintenance personnel are on the premises performing necessary maintenance work. Such maintenance work shall be conducted after notice to and approval by the Douglas County Fire Department and Douglas County Emergency E-911. A fire watch may be required during the time the water-based fire protection system or fire alarm system is removed from service, and shall remain in place until such time as the systems are returned to full functioning capacity.

813:
(a) Fire-fighting accessibility.
(1) Accessibility of buildings for fire-fighting equipment:
a. Reasonable accessibility shall be provided to and around all buildings for firefighting equipment, including ladder trucks on multiple-story projects. Accessibility shall be approved by the fire chief or his designee.
b. Accessibility for firefighter's equipment shall be maintained throughout all stages of construction.
c. Minimum widths of access roads, excluding parking, shall be 20 feet. Minimum turning radius shall be 32 feet. All access roads and fire lanes shall be capable of supporting the loads of fire apparatus and shall have a minimum of 13) feet, six inches of vertical clearance.
d. All access roads in excess of 150 feet in length shall be provided with an approved area for turning around fire apparatus.
e. Gates securing fire apparatus access shall be provided with an automatic gate-opening device if the gates are controlled by electronic means. An approved siren operated sensor shall activate the gate-opening device.
f. Gates securing fire apparatus access shall be a minimum 14 feet in clear width for divided lanes and 20 feet for a single lane. Gate shall be swing or sliding type. Fire access lanes shall be straight and have no turns for 50 feet on both sides of security gate.
g. Additional fire apparatus access may be required based on the fire chief or his designee's opinion.
(2) Aerial fire apparatus access road:
a. Buildings or portions of buildings or facilities exceeding 30 feet in height above the lowest level of fire department vehicle access shall be provided with approved fire apparatus roads capable of accommodating fire department aerial apparatus. Overhead utility and power lines shall not be located within the aerial fire apparatus access roadway.
b. Fire apparatus access roads shall have a minimum unobstructed width of 26 feet in the immediate vicinity of any building or portion of building more than 30 feet in height.
c. At least one of the required access roads meeting this condition shall be located within a minimum of 15 feet and a maximum of 30 feet from the building, and shall be positioned parallel to one entire side of the building.
d. Commercial and industrial buildings exceeding 30 feet or three stories in height shall have at least three means of fire apparatus access for each structure.
(b) Fire hydrant installation prior to construction.
(1) Water mains and fire hydrants, shall be installed, under water pressure and ready for fire fighting, before any combustible materials are brought onto construction sites.
(2) All fire hydrants, fittings, valves and fire department connections shall be approved by the Douglasville-Douglas County Water and Sewer Authority and the Douglas County Fire Department. Fire department connections shall not be less than 18 inches nor more than 36 inches above the level of the adjoining ground or paving. The thread of such connections shall be uniform with that used by the fire department.
(3) The size and shape of the operation nut, as well as the direction the hydrant stem operates, shall be uniform the hydrant stem operates, shall be uniform with construction standards and specifications of the Douglasville-Douglas County Water and Sewer Authority for hydrants and for water distribution systems.
(c) Fire hydrant installation standards for minimum size water mains and spacing of fire hydrants for all new construction.
(1) In single-family residential subdivisions, at least eight-inch ductile iron pipe shall be installed. Fire hydrants shall be spaced not to exceed 400 feet. Three-way fire hydrants shall be used.
(2) In multi-family residential subdivisions, multi-family apartment complexes, industrial areas and commercial areas, (including but not limited to motels, hotels, nursing homes, hospitals, education buildings, all office buildings and churches) at least eight-inch ductile iron pipe water mains shall be installed to provide a minimum water flow of 1,000 gallons per minute. Larger mains and flows may be required by the building official or his designee. Fire hydrants shall be three-way hydrants and shall be spaced not to exceed 400 feet, with additional hydrants located as necessary, to permit all portions of the exterior buildings and combustible storage to be reached by hose lays of not more than 400 feet. Fire hydrant locations shall be approved by the building official or his designee to allow fire fighting equipment to be placed within 15 feet of said hydrants.
(3) In mobile home parks, fire hydrants shall be spaced not to exceed 400 feet, with a minimum of an eight-inch ductile iron pipe waterline, which shall be installed to provide a water flow of at least 700 gallons per minute.
(4) Prior to any preliminary subdivision plat submission for approval, the applicant shall obtain approval of the building official or his designee for the spacing of all fire hydrants, main size and water flows.
(5) No pipe smaller than a standard eight inch in diameter shall be used to supply more than one hydrant or one hydrant on dead-end mains over 500 feet but not exceeding 999 feet, and no smaller than a ten inch in diameter for dead-end main for 1,000 feet or more.
(6) No pipe smaller than a standard eight inch in diameter shall be used to supply one hydrant and automatic extinguishing systems.
(7) No pipe smaller than a standard eight inch in diameter shall be used to supply more than one hydrant and automatic extinguishing systems on looped mains of 1,000 feet.
(d) [Deviation.] In all of the above requirements in Section 42-45, in the event any deviation is desired to be made, a request for such deviation shall be submitted to and approved by the Douglas County Fire Department in writing. The fire department chief and/or his or her designee, said designee including but not limited to the fire marshal, shall have the authority to make such approval on behalf of the Douglas County Fire Department.
(Ord. No. O-04-42, § 1, 10-4-04; Ord. No. O-2022-10, § 12, 3-7-22; Ord. No. O-2023-11, § 1, 3-6-23)
